name: NJ-01

model.rationale: Norcross holds a D+10 seat with a large cash advantage and no meaningful outside spending against him, while Galdo has raised only about $11,000. Markets price the race around 95% Democratic, consistent with fundamentals pointing to a roughly 20-point margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Norcross or a strong national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Donald Norcross is seeking another term in a South Jersey district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.4 million in the bank after raising more than $1.6 million, while Republican Damon Galdo has raised about $11,000 and has no outside support on either side. No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets put Norcross's chances near 95%, and the fundamentals point to a margin of roughly twenty points. With the incumbent running, heavily outspending his opponent, and no visible outside opposition, the race sits firmly in the safe Democratic category, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a genuine contest.
